newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end off on U.S. rate rise fears.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end off on U.S. rate rise fears.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed softer in thin trade on Thursday with the bolsa tracking Wall Street lower on fears that the U.S. Federal Reserve could raise interest rates at its meeting next week, said dealers.
The bolsa is seen holding steady at the opening with turnover remaining light, they said.
"Everything will be quiet until the Fed meeting on Tuesday," said one dealer.
The 40-share index closed down 0.5 percent at 111.49 points. The general index shed 0.13 percent to 5,218.22 points in turnover of 10.4 billion pesos.
Chilean-issued ADRs were hurt by Wall Street's slide on comments by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan stressing the Fed's need to act pre-emptively to keep inflation low.
Greenspan's comments apart, dealers reported little foreign interest in Chilean stocks.
Losers included electricity utility Enersis which tumbled on profit-taking by foreign investors, they said.
"But it is now attractively priced so the stock could recover next week," said one trader.
Other losers included copper products maker Madeco, down 3.29 percent at 1,030 pesos and drug company LabChile which shed 1.12 percent to 440 pesos.
Winners included telecom Entel, up 1.48 percent at 2,750 pesos, brewery CCU, up 0.65 percent at 1,540 pesos and winery Concha y Toro which rose 0.44 percent to 228 pesos.
